root_cause.text: The iwlwifi MLD teardown path failed to cancel the per-vif delayed work `mlo_scan_start_wk` when a station interface was disconnected/moved down, allowing a queued work item to later run after interface state changes or after the `vif` had been freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(mld->wiphy, &mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk);` from `iwl_mld_cleanup_vif()` into `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down()`, and the CVE text says the work was “not canceled on disconnection,” which could cause an “init-after-queue issue” after `drv_change_interface` and a “use-after-free” if executed after `vif` free.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The iwlwifi MLD code failed to cancel the per-vif delayed work item `mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk` during normal interface teardown/disconnection, allowing a queued work handler to run after the vif state had changed or the vif had been freed.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(mld->wiphy, &mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk);` from `iwl_mld_cleanup_vif()` and adds the same cancel call in `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down()`, while the CVE text says the work “is not canceled on disconnection” and can cause “init-after-queue” and “use-after-free” if it runs after `drv_change_interface` or after `vif` free.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence and CVE do support that `mlo_scan_start_wk` was not canceled on disconnection and could lead to init-after-queue/use-after-free, but the proposed root cause is inconsistent with the patch diff. The diff shows the cancel call was removed from `iwl_mld_cleanup_vif()` and added in `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down()`, meaning the bug is specifically that cancellation was missing from the teardown/disconnection path and needed to be moved earlier, not simply that “normal interface teardown/disconnection” failed in a generic sense. The root cause also does not explain the mechanism clearly enough: why an already-queued delayed work item can run after `drv_change_interface` or after `vif` free.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove explicit cancellation of the MLO scan start delayed work from VIF cleanup.
intent_record.what: The call to `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(mld->wiphy, &mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk);` was removed from `iwl_mld_cleanup_vif()`, leaving the key cleanup and `CLEANUP_STRUCT(mld_vif);` intact.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the VIF cleanup path no longer explicitly cancels the `mlo_scan_start_wk` delayed work before tearing down `mld_vif`. This changes cleanup behavior for that work item and may allow its cancellation to be handled elsewhere or no longer be needed at this point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending MLO scan-start work during station state teardown to avoid stale delayed work executing after the state change.
intent_record.what: In iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down(), a new call to wiphy_delayed_work_cancel() was added to cancel mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk alongside the existing EMLSR work cancellations.
intent_record.how: When a station is moved down in state, any pending MLO scan-start delayed work is now explicitly stopped, preventing that work item from running after the interface has transitioned out of the relevant state.

This line shows the pattern used in teardown to cancel delayed work. The missing equivalent cancellation for mlo_scan_start_wk is the direct bug, leaving stale delayed work pending across station state teardown.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the teardown path for station/interface state transitions, and it already cancels multiple per-vif works in the down path. In `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down()`, when a station leaves AUTHORIZED->ASSOC it does `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(mld->wiphy, &mld_vif->emlsr.prevent_done_wk);`, `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(...tmp_non_bss_done_wk);`, `wiphy_work_cancel(...unblock_tpt_wk);`, and `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(...check_tpt_wk);`. However, the vulnerable work from the root cause, `mlo_scan_start_wk`, is not present anywhere in this snippet, so the exact vulnerable construct is absent here. Because the shown code already contains explicit cancellation handling in the teardown path and there is no visible `mlo_scan_start_wk` omission to indicate the bug, this commit version cannot be marked as containing the described bug. It therefore appears fixed with respect to the cancel-on-teardown pattern described, at least in the provided function body.
